description.narrative: 350 Global is seeking funding for our global mobilization, "Draw the Line." The funding will contribute towards rallying thousands in cities and villages worldwide to demand a world where we can speak up for our rights, where people and nature are safe, and wherebig polluters help pay to fix the climate crisis. The impacts of climate change are worsening by the year, and food and energy costs are rising; meanwhile, a handful of billionaires are profiting from propping up industries that pollute our land, air, and water. It couldn’t be clearer that our future is on the line. This September, hundreds of thousands of people around the world will Draw the Line against this unfairness. We will celebrate a global weekend of action, with a series of mobilizations large and small, between September 19–21, 2025. Across the world, we will bring people together in a massive show of strength, solidarity, resistance, and celebration to demand real, urgent, and decisive action from world leaders. Together, we will call for a better world for ourselves,our children, and our communities: a world with clean, affordable energy for all. 350 Global and a growing number of organizations are coming together to make this weekend of actions powerful enough to capture public attention, transform the narrative, and challenge current political stances in the lead-up to COP30. 1. A Critical Juncture for Climate and Democracy As the world moves toward COP30 in Brazil, the climate crisis has deepened alarmingly. The past year has seen record-breaking heat waves, catastrophic floods, devastating wildfires, and prolonged droughts across every continent. And yet, governments are failing to approach COP30 with the strong ambition needed. Nationally Determined Contributions(NDCs) remain underwhelming. Key national policies are failing to reflect the urgency that the climate crisis demands. Globally, a resurgence of climate-denying political forces has weakened international ambition. While the Trump administration has had a chilling effect on climate leadership, challenges exist around the globe. For example, in Brazil, while the Lula administration has slowed deforestation, it has simultaneously supported aggressive fossil fuel expansion. In France, Germany, and other EU countries, far-right parties with anti-climate agendas are gaining strength. In Indonesia, the recent election of a right-wing government has accelerated coal development under the banner of energy sovereignty. In Nigeria, despite abundant solar potential, the government continues to favor fossil fuel development, stall solar expansion, and delay a just transition. Globally, the rise of authoritarianism and fossil-fueled nationalism threatens to derail the gains made under the Paris Agreement. This is a moment in which the climate emergency is directly linked to democratic erosion. To defend both people and the planet, we must Draw the Line. 2. The Transformative Power of Public Action Time and time again, mass public action has shaped the trajectory of the climate movement. The 2014 People’s Climate March in New York City brought over 400,000 people to the streets in the US(and millions in solidarity events around the world!), catalyzing new political commitments and generating momentum in support of the Paris Agreement. The 2019 global climate strikes drew over 7 million people from more than 150 countries, led by youth demanding intergenerational justice. The Stop EACOP mobilizations have delayed a major oil project in Uganda and Tanzania, while the 2024 March to End Fossil Fuels played a role in slowing LNG expansion in the US. This September, we will channel that spirit again. From faith communities and students to nurses, transit workers, and elders, from the barrios of Colombia to the coastlines of the Philippines, from Berlin to Nairobi to New Orleans, people will rise to Draw the Line, championing a set of interconnected demands on: ● Energy: Build a clean energy system: stop fossil fuels, fast and fair ● Finance: Fund the Future, Not the Crisis ● Justice: Center Workersand Communities ● Democracy: Protect People, Not Polluters ● Peace: Defend Rights, Freedom, and Peace ● Land: Restore Our Relationship with Earth These demands are deliberately broad: to fit a range of contexts and resonate with different organizations and communities across the world. Together, we will Draw the Line to show world leaders, fossil fuel CEOs, and finance leaders the thread thatconnects these: the urgent need to end fossil fuel expansion and finance a just transition to clean energy. These actions aren’t merely symbolic. They will be designed with care to shape public opinion, attract media coverage, shift electoral platforms, and inspire local policy changes. They will demonstrate that the call for climate justice is not a fringe concern but a mainstream, multi-sectoral demand. Perhaps most importantly, by creating a moment of collective agency, building community and celebrating our interlinked hopes and dreams, these actions will Draw the Line towards hope and solidarity in an age of fear and fragmentation. 3. Strategy and Tactics: A Global, Distributed, Creative Action 350.org, alongside a growing number of diverse organizations and grassroots movements, is organizing the Draw the Line mobilization this September to drive impact at a global scale through: ● A Global Weekend of Action (Sept 19-21): A long weekend of synchronized mobilizations, massive public demonstrations, and community-based actions. We expect 500+ actions across the world, from major cities to rural communities. ● Creative Tactics: Drawing red and green lines in public spaces (human chains, chalk or paint lines, banners, and fabric), staging solar cookouts and clean energy fairs, public art installations, street theatre, and ceremonies led by Indigenous and faith leaders. ● High-Impact Communications and Media Outreach: A multilingual, culturally resonant media campaign including press outreach, op-eds, video shorts, influencer toolkits, drone footage, music, and viral social media content. We will proactively place stories and interviews with frontline leaders in top-tier global and regional outlets. We expect 500+ media hits across national, regional, and global outlets. Through massive digital engagement, we are aiming for over 10 million impressions and thousands of user-generated posts. ● North-South Solidarity: Through coordinated actions in the Global North and South, we will demonstrate the growing public demand for loss and damage finance, fossil fuel phaseout, and clean energy investments - climate action, anchored in justice and global equity. This will strengthen grassroots infrastructure and build new partnerships, cross-sector collaborations, and enhanced organizing capacity for the long term.

participating-org.narrative: Stichting 350 Global is a Dutch foundation (Stichting) based in Amsterdam, registered with the Dutch Chamber of Commerce under number 93988656. The foundation was established on May 28, 2024, with the objective of contributing to global climate justice through nature conservation and environmental awareness.Its primary activities focus on nature conservation (SBI-code 91042), and it is aligned with the international 350.org movement, advocating for reducing atmospheric CO₂ levels and promoting sustainable solutions. The organization operates as a non-profit and is governed by a board of directors acting jointly.
